openings.claim: The sampling log alone can make a limited review reproducible by preserving selection reasons before label access; it does not establish deployment readiness.
openings.delta: Change the log's action from recording retrospective inspection reasons to committing each record identifier, priority criterion and intended decision relevance before access. The carrier remains the supplied spreadsheet or local script. Prioritize flagged rows in the slice already losing two and the improvement slice with annotator disagreements; fix identifier order within priorities. Record returned labels, unavailable attempts, elapsed time and allowance consumed.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, an ordinary retrospective sampling log using the same priority rule, pre-access commitments should expose selection-rule deviations and let a replay distinguish planned selection from post-result justification. Decision accuracy may be unchanged or worse; priority alone cannot resolve remaining labels.
openings.probe: Use the two matched copies, one per log variant, with the same withheld four rows. Allocate at most twenty-five minutes per variant and twenty minutes to replay and key comparison, totaling seventy. Permit at most sixteen returned adjudications per copy; log withheld attempts without charging allowance. Freeze each supplied-rule advance, reject or unresolved report, affected slices and complete access ledger before opening the full-label key. Compare reconstructable selection reasons, deviations, allowance accounting and decision agreement with the key. Report unresolved whenever unadjudicated label possibilities can change the acceptance result; retain the original four-gain and two-loss thresholds.
assumptions: The supplied records permit deterministic identifier ordering and identifying flagged rows in the relevant slices.
The replay comparison is descriptive; two runs cannot establish reliable general performance.

Defeat conditions include equally reconstructable rival reasons, no exposed deviations, poorer supported decisions, or insufficient time to finish replay; missing or withheld labels may force unresolved.

assessment: This opening transfers the second parent's record-to-reason association into pre-access commitments. Its potential benefit is auditable selection and explicit uncertainty, not a guaranteed advance decision. Supplied evidence does not establish the effect.
